leaders.name: Keyanna Boka
leaders.note: Appears in the WKU Archives regents index as student regent, 2013. Plaque spells the first name KEYANNA; the archives index reads Boka, Keyana - confirm which is correct.
profile: Boka, the outgoing executive vice president, was elected 2013-14 SGA president on 4 April 2013 with 626 votes (47 percent), beating administrative vice president Cain Alvey (419 votes) and Austin Wingate (300). Five days later the Judicial Council voted 3-2 to disqualify her after Alvey, the runner-up who stood to become president if she were removed, complained that a self-promotional email had gone to Honors College students at her request. Boka appealed to Howard Bailey, WKU's vice president for Student Affairs, who reinstated her; the Judicial Council declined to contest his ruling in an emergency meeting on 16 April, with Chief Justice Seth Church calling the intervention "a serious infringement on our autonomy" and Boka countering that the council itself had conflicts of interest.

In office, Boka's fall 2013 senate created a new international student senate seat for Navitas/ESL students and finalized a $125,000 budget, part of which sent her and executive vice president Mark Reeves on a Washington, D.C. higher-education lobbying trip. She fielded student anger over new two-tier priority registration rules at a November open forum with Provost Gordon Emslie, and announced the permanent closure of Thompson Complex North Wing, long slated for demolition. A senate attempt to reverse SGA's support for the Talisman's student fee was struck down by the Judicial Council as unconstitutional, as was the underlying 2005 policy.

In spring 2014 Boka organized a Frankfort rally against a $1.8 million state budget cut to WKU and opposed a senate amendment stripping the president's sole power to appoint Judicial Council justices, which was sent back to committee after the council found too few senators had been present to pass it. At the year's final meeting she announced a 4.8 percent tuition increase for the coming year, and the senate passed a resolution backing a Good Samaritan policy to protect students who called 911 during drug or alcohol overdoses.

events.title: Fall election drew 564 voters, created international seat
events.body: A total of 564 voters cast ballots in the fall SGA election. A referendum creating the Navitas/ESL international student senate seat passed with 310 of 426 votes, or 73 percent. Six freshman senators were elected out of seven candidates, with Jay Todd Richey taking 27 percent of the vote, and most college senate seats went to unopposed candidates.

events.title: SGA finalized $125,000 budget
events.body: SGA finalized a $125,000 budget for the 2013-14 year, funded from student tuition at about $6.25 per student, after a planned funding increase did not come through. The organizational aid committee was allotted $30,000, with campus organizations able to receive up to $500 each. The executive discretionary fund held $5,900, part of which covered a Washington, D.C. higher education lobbying trip by Boka and Reeves.

events.title: Priority registration complaints spurred open forum
events.body: Student complaints over new two-tier priority registration rules, including a 16-credit-hour cap during the priority period, pushed SGA to schedule a Nov. 12 open forum with Provost Gordon Emslie. Honors College seniors told senator Tyler Scaff some were considering dropping the honors major over the change. Boka said she had no official stance yet, though SGA had earlier approved the change through Reeves's vote at University Senate.

events.title: Thompson Complex North Wing set to close permanently
events.body: Boka announced at the Tuesday SGA meeting that Thompson Complex North Wing, home to the biology and chemistry departments, would close permanently the next semester because the building could not be maintained over the winter. The building had been labeled for demolition since 2005, and its demolition along with renovation of the Center Wing was the university's top capital priority before the Kentucky General Assembly.

events.title: Judicial Council voided Talisman fee stance reversal
events.body: After the yearbook's budget was cut to $127,000, senator Chris Costa moved at the Nov. 19 meeting to revoke SGA's stance supporting a $9 student fee for the Talisman that students had approved on a 2005 ballot, and two-thirds of SGA voted to reverse the stance. The Judicial Council ruled Costa's motion unconstitutional on Nov. 21, and also ruled the original 2005 policy unconstitutional because it was never passed according to SGA policy. Talisman editors then met with Boka and SGA members to discuss long-term funding options.

events.title: SGA reconvened, planned Frankfort rally against budget cuts
events.body: At the first spring meeting, Boka announced a planned trip to Frankfort called "Rally for Retention" in response to WKU's $1.8 million state budget cut, with speeches and one-on-one meetings with legislators. Reeves warned that tough budget cuts were coming, and the body reviewed a proposal to revise the change-of-major advising process. Five members had resigned the previous semester, leaving the legislative research and public relations chairs among the vacant seats.

events.title: Executive Council nullified judicial appointment amendment
events.body: An amendment stripping the SGA president's sole power to appoint judicial council justices and raising the number of justices to seven passed at the Tuesday meeting, over Boka's objection that it bypassed presidential appointment and the senate. After the meeting the Executive Council reviewed the constitution and determined too few senators had attended for the vote to count, sending the amendment back to first read. The SGA office also temporarily moved to Garrett after flooding in Cravens.

events.title: Final meeting passed Good Samaritan resolution, funding bills
events.body: At the last meeting of the semester, Boka announced students would face a 4.8 percent tuition increase, about $209 more per semester for most, alongside a $4.2 million increase in student financial assistance. The Senate suspended its bylaws to pass a slate of bills funding Summer Term assistance, student organizations, student research and an Earth Week planting party. Resolution 6-14-S passed in support of adopting a Good Samaritan Policy protecting students who call 911 during drug or alcohol overdoses.

events.title: Senate passed international student seat amendment
events.body: President Keyana Boka and executive vice president Mark Reeves authored a constitutional amendment adding a senate seat for Navitas or English as a Second Language international students. The Judicial Council had ruled an earlier version unconstitutional, but after a revision in an emergency meeting the Senate passed it with only two votes against. Boka said it would make WKU's SGA the first student government in the state with an international senate seat.

events.title: Presidential debate drew full field of candidates
events.body: Ahead of the spring 2013 election, outgoing president Cory Dodds opened a debate in Ransdell Hall Auditorium among presidential candidates Cain Alvey, Keyana Boka and Austin Wingate, plus executive vice presidential candidates Brad Cockrel and Mark Reeves and administrative vice presidential candidate Nicki Seay. Boka said SGA members needed better training in their roles, Alvey said the presidency's responsibilities went beyond the constitution, and Wingate, a former Speaker of the Senate, called for better representation across student groups.

events.title: Executive Council floated plus/minus grading, set fall calendar
events.body: At the Executive Council's weekly meeting, Executive Vice President Mark Reeves reported that the University Senate Council had discussed reviving a plus/minus grading system and that Provost Gordon Emslie was interested in SGA's support. The council set a Nov. 9 Picnic with the President for the presidents' council and deans, and swore in Samantha Johnson to an executive cabinet seat vacated by the resignation of Keith Watson.

events.title: SGA reviewed 24-hour dining, grading and registration proposals
events.body: SGA gave first read to a proposal for a 24-hour on-campus dining option, with the Organizational Aid Committee sponsoring the resolution and assistant vice president for auxiliary services Gary Meszaros set to attend the next meeting. Reeves told senators Provost Gordon Emslie was reviving a plus/minus grading proposal and had brought priority registration and major-declaration changes to University Senate.

events.title: Herald editorial faulted SGA over registration policy
events.body: A Herald editorial accused SGA of failing to represent students on the new priority-registration hour cap, saying executive vice president Mark Reeves voted for the policy at University Senate on Sept. 10 without SGA questioning or debating it first. The editorial argued SGA had one job, representing students, and had not done it on this issue.

events.title: Mid-year budget report showed $46,883 surplus
events.body: SGA's mid-year budget report showed a $46,883.62 surplus on its $125,000 budget. The Senate approved Bill 3-14-S allocating organizational funds and suspended its bylaws to pass Resolution 3-14-S supporting WKU's participation in the Campus Pride Index, and approved Hannah Neeper, Elizabeth Gribbins and AJ Stewart as new senators as six senate seats remained open.

senate.note: Twenty-six student senators were elected in the April 2013 spring election alongside the executive officers. Executive Council minutes for 10 Sept 2013 list cabinet members Sarah Hazelip, Hannah Garland, Paige Settles, Laura Harper and Brad Cockrel alongside Boka, Reeves and Seay; Samantha Johnson was sworn in that night to a seat vacated by Keith Watson's resignation.

leaders.name: Nicki Taylor
leaders.note: The chambers plaque carries two consecutive plates for this year: "Janet 'Nicki' Seay" and "Nicki Taylor." Herald coverage shows one continuous officeholder, not a succession: she opened the year as "Nicki Seay" (Herald, 28 Aug and 25 Sep 2014), was already being called "Nicki Taylor" by the very next issue on 15 Oct 2014, and was still SGA president under that name through the 2 Apr 2015 election that chose her successor - no election, resignation or hand-off for a second officeholder appears anywhere in that span. Treated here as a single president who changed her surname partway through the term.
profile: Nicki Seay had been SGA's Legislative Research Chair in 2012-13 and ran successfully for administrative vice president in the spring 2013 election. She took office as SGA president in August 2014, a Crofton senior, alongside Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler and Executive Vice President Nolan Miles, and named student involvement, retention and graduation her priorities. Her administration opened the year by expanding SGA's summer and winter need-based scholarship program from $6,000 to $21,000.

By the middle of October 2014 the Herald was referring to the same sitting president as Nicki Taylor; no election or resignation separates the two names in the paper's coverage. As Taylor, she presided over a fall senate that voted down a nonsectarian prayer resolution, saw its smoke-free campus resolution vetoed by the Executive Cabinet and sustained on a failed override vote, and passed a resolution backing changes to the campus alcohol policy. She addressed WKU's December 2014 commencement as SGA president, telling graduates, "You have the rest of your life to look forward to."

In the spring semester the senate under Taylor passed a limited-smoking-campus resolution and a resolution backing a $10 million parking garage funded by a new student fee; President Gary Ransdell responded formally to both. She also sat, by virtue of the office, on the WKU Board of Regents, and abstained from an Executive Council vote on the smoking measure because of that seat. Her term ended with the 2 April 2015 election of Jay Todd Richey as her successor.

events.title: An election result challenged and upheld
events.body: Anonymous accusations alleged Jay Todd Richey had breached election codes on poster placement. The judicial council warned him against future violations and confirmed he had rightfully won.

events.title: SGA opened the year with a $21,000 scholarship program
events.body: SGA began the year under new president Nicki Seay, a Crofton senior, working alongside Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler and Executive Vice President Nolan Miles. The association expanded its summer and winter term need-based scholarship program from the previous year's $6,000 to $21,000, funded in part by an anonymous donation. Seay named student involvement, retention and graduation her first priorities.

events.title: Downing Student Union celebrated its community opening
events.body: WKU held a ceremonial community opening for Downing Student Union after a two-year, $49 million renovation; the building had opened to students the week before. Students paid $36 million of the cost through a $70-per-semester fee, and the renovation began as an SGA initiative in 2011. SGA President Nicki Seay attended alongside President Gary Ransdell and other officials.

events.title: Fall election drew 742 voters and seated 17 senators
events.body: SGA announced its fall election results around 12:20 a.m. in the Senate Chamber of Downing Student Union. There were 742 voters and 17 senators were elected, including three freshman senators led by Emily Pride with 281 votes. President Nicki Seay called the election very competitive, noting not everyone who ran won a seat.

events.title: Senate defeated a nonsectarian prayer policy resolution
events.body: After more than 20 minutes of debate, the senate defeated Resolution 4-14-F, which would have supported adopting the University Senate's nonsectarian public prayer policy for university-sponsored events. President Nicki Taylor said the senate was split three ways among nonsectarian prayer, sectarian prayer and no prayer at all. The same night, senators passed Bill 9-14-F allocating $250 in organizational aid to the Phi Gamma Delta fraternity.

events.title: Executive Cabinet vetoed the smoke-free campus resolution
events.body: The senate passed Resolution 11-14-F, supporting a smoke-free campus, on a 14-10 vote, but the SGA Executive Cabinet vetoed it after the meeting. Chief of Staff Seth Church argued it was unfair to ban smoking for students required to live on campus for two years. Senators retained the power to override the veto with a two-thirds vote.

events.title: Veto override failed; alcohol policy resolution passed
events.body: At the final meeting of the fall semester, the senate failed to overturn the Executive Cabinet's veto of the smoke-free resolution, and President Nicki Taylor read the cabinet's official veto statement citing enforcement, housing requirements and practicality. The senate then passed Resolution 13-14-F, supporting amendments to WKU's alcohol policy and Student Code of Conduct to let students 21 and older purchase and possess alcohol on campus. Co-author Jody Dahmer called the existing policy ineffective and hard to enforce fairly.

events.title: President Taylor addressed December graduates
events.body: SGA President Nicki Taylor spoke at WKU's December commencement, telling graduates to celebrate what they had accomplished: "You have the rest of your life to look forward to." She had opened the year in August under her previous surname, Seay, and was going by Taylor in Herald coverage by mid-October.

events.title: President Taylor abstained on smoking vote as a sitting regent
events.body: The Bowling Green Daily News reported that Nicki Taylor, in addition to serving as SGA president, sat on the WKU Board of Regents, and abstained from an Executive Council vote on the smoking-campus proposal because of that seat.

events.title: Limited smoking campus resolution passed 13-11
events.body: SGA passed Resolution 1-15-S, supporting a limited smoking campus, by a 13-11 vote. The resolution would restrict tobacco use to 39 designated areas that the Administrative Council would gradually phase out over three years, while leaving electronic cigarettes and smokeless tobacco unrestricted. Co-author Seth Church said it was roughly the fifth version of the resolution since the smoking debate began the previous semester.

events.title: SGA backed a $10 million parking garage funded by a $30 fee
events.body: SGA passed a resolution supporting construction of a new parking structure on part of Creason Lot, funded by a $30-per-semester tuition increase. Authors Zach Jones, Brian Chism and Nathan Cherry estimated the roughly 500-car garage would take about 18 months to build. Chief of Staff Seth Church objected that the plan was rushed and left out regional campuses.

events.title: Ransdell formally responded to four SGA resolutions
events.body: President Gary Ransdell emailed faculty and staff his official response to four SGA resolutions on limited smoking, campus alcohol sales, a new parking structure and a student fee for WKU Student Legal Services. He announced a six-person ad hoc committee to implement a limited smoking campus by the end of 2017 and a restaurant in the Garrett Conference Center that could serve beer in the evenings. He said the parking and legal services fees would need Board of Regents and Council on Postsecondary Education approval.

events.title: Jay Todd Richey won the SGA presidency, 874 votes to 524
events.body: Jay Todd Richey defeated senator Brian Chism for SGA president, 63 percent to 37 percent, or 874 votes to 524, with results announced about 20 minutes after TopNet polls closed at 11:59 p.m. Wednesday. Nolan Miles ran unopposed for a second term as executive vice president, and Liz Koehler won the administrative vice president race with 66 percent over J. William Berry. Twenty of 34 senatorial candidates won seats.

executive.name: Nicki Taylor
executive.note: Took office in August 2014 as Nicki Seay; called Nicki Taylor in coverage from mid-October 2014 on.

senate.note: 17 senators were elected in the September 2014 fall election out of 742 votes cast; the spring 2015 election filled 20 of 34 contested senate seats.

leaders.name: Jay Todd Richey
leaders.note: Won amid anonymous complaints that he had breached election codes on poster placement. The Judicial Council warned him but confirmed the result stood.
profile: Richey opened his first term in fall 2015 "leaving behind the Postergate controversy" of the spring election, saying he had "about a hundred things" he wanted to do. His priorities included MyCampusToo, a campaign initiative to bring underrepresented students into SGA, more outreach to international students and the regional campuses, and stronger communication between the executive cabinet and senate. He also oversaw a student competition to name the new pub coming to the Garrett Conference Center, a product of the alcohol-policy change SGA had supported the previous year.

In September he championed the senate's resolution disapproving of how the Confucius Institute building was approved, writing in a letter to the Herald that the contract was signed in China before the Board of Regents voted and that many controversial details were never disclosed. He rejected warnings that the vote made "powerful enemies," saying he hoped it sent a message that "accountability and transparency should always be top priorities" at WKU, while noting he respected Ransdell and would keep working with him.

In April 2016 Richey won reelection with 1,497 of 2,341 presidential votes, becoming a two-term president in a high-turnout election announced after midnight in the Downing Student Union senate chambers. "It's a tremendous honor to be elected the first time," he said, "but a second time is verification of promises kept." His running mate Kate Hart won executive vice president and MyCampusToo chairwoman Hannah Neeper won administrative vice president, keeping his allies in the executive branch for 2016-17. A March 2017 Herald profile noted the win made him WKU SGA's first two-term president since 1988 and one of only three since 1974.

events.title: SGA budget fell by $19,500
events.body: SGA's budget dropped $19,500 from the previous year, largely because a $15,000 private donation was not repeated and the university cut another $4,500 in reallocations. Organizational funding took the hardest hit, losing $9,000, and scholarship pools for Academic Affairs and Student Affairs each fell by more than $5,000. Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reallocated $4,000 from organizational aid back into scholarships to soften the loss.

events.title: Chief Justice resigned after censure hearing backlash
events.body: The Judicial Council unanimously declined to censure senator John Winstead, whom it had investigated over an "impeach Ransdell" sign and a mocking Facebook post about President Ransdell, ruling his actions were protected free speech. Winstead called the fact he was investigated at all "the problem I'm objecting to." Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell then announced she would step down at the end of the semester, saying the council had been publicly ridiculed and lacked support from fellow SGA members.

events.title: Administration overrode student vote on pub name
events.body: Richey announced that administrators had renamed the future Garrett Conference Center pub "Topper Grill and Pub," setting aside the name students chose in SGA's "Dub the Pub" contest, Topper Tavern. Richey said Ransdell wanted to downplay the alcohol theme and called himself "very disappointed," saying the move made SGA question how much the administration listened to students. At the same meeting SGA introduced the RAVE Guardian campus safety app.

events.title: Ransdell announced retirement amid state budget cuts
events.body: President Gary Ransdell announced he would step down as WKU's ninth president on June 30, 2017, triggering a presidential search. The announcement came the same week new Gov. Matt Bevin ordered an immediate 4.5 percent cut to WKU's state funding and proposed a 9 percent cut, with future funding shifted to a performance-based pool. The changes framed much of SGA's advocacy for the rest of the year.

events.title: Senate opposed state tuition-freeze bill
events.body: The senate approved Resolution 2-16-S opposing Kentucky Senate Bill 75, which would have frozen resident tuition at 2015-16 levels for four years. Richey argued such freezes were "dangerous risks" that could wreck universities and cost students more in the long run. At the same meeting, Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reported an expected 4.5 percent cut to SGA's own budget, about $1,301.

events.title: Senators lobbied legislators in Frankfort
events.body: SGA members traveled to Frankfort to lobby against state budget cuts that could slash WKU funding by as much as 9 percent, meeting with eight state officials. Senators pressed for smaller cuts and restoration of need-based aid, citing figures that about 15,000 students were denied need-based financial aid the prior year. Both chambers of the General Assembly recognized SGA for its participation.

events.title: Ransdell declined SGA's meningitis vaccine mandate
events.body: Richey read aloud a letter from Ransdell responding to Resolution 6-15-F, passed the previous semester, which supported requiring meningitis vaccinations for incoming freshmen living on campus starting with the class of 2020. Ransdell wrote that the university would highly recommend vaccination but "stop short of requiring it," citing a $143.77 cost for uninsured students at the Graves-Gilbert Clinic.

events.title: Senate passed guidelines for WKU's tenth president
events.body: The senate approved a resolution by John Winstead and Richey outlining what students wanted in WKU's tenth president, which Richey planned to use in his role on the presidential search committee. After debate, senators amended the sustainability clause to target improving WKU's AASHE STARS rating and voted to remove language about Jonesville "reparations" entirely, after disputing whether reparations or restitution was the right term.

events.title: Richey reelected in one of highest-turnout elections
events.body: Students reelected Jay Todd Richey as SGA president with 64 percent of the vote over Braxton Powell, in one of the highest-turnout elections in the association's history with 2,442 voters. Kate Hart, an Academic Affairs chairwoman and Richey's running mate, won executive vice president. Richey called the win "verification of promises kept."

events.title: Richey outlined fall goals, MyCampusToo launch
events.body: Opening his first term, President Jay Todd Richey said he wanted more executive-cabinet and senate communication and more outreach to international students and regional campuses, and confirmed his campaign initiative MyCampusToo would launch that semester. Executive Vice President Nolan Miles said he would push senators to sit on university committees and revive the Dine with Decision Makers event.

events.title: Senate voted to disapprove Confucius Institute approval process
events.body: The Student Senate voted overwhelmingly to pass a resolution disapproving of how the Confucius Institute building project was approved, after President Gary Ransdell signed the contract in China in December 2014 and the Board of Regents, including the Student Regent, voted on it more than a month later without full details disclosed. Richey said the vote was not meant to set a precedent beyond ensuring the Board had full information before acting.

events.title: Senate backed meningitis vaccine requirement, amended bylaws
events.body: The Senate unanimously passed Resolution 6-15-F supporting a meningococcal meningitis vaccination requirement for incoming freshmen in on-campus housing beginning with the class of 2020, and unanimously passed Bill 10-15-F amending SGA's bylaws. Richey reported that his fall listening tours of the regional campuses had gone well and turned up how different those campuses were from main campus.

officers.name: Page Settles
officers.note: Listed among non-voting officers in attendance at the 1 Dec 2015 executive cabinet meeting.

senate.note: At the 1 Dec 2015 executive cabinet meeting, Miles and Koehler disagreed with then-Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell's call for a separate Judicial Council adviser; Luttrell resigned two days later.

documents.title: Executive Cabinet meeting minutes, 1 December 2015
documents.summary: The Richey administration's own record of a fall 2015 cabinet meeting: the voting and non-voting officers then serving, a discussion of a possible independent Judicial Council adviser two days before Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell's resignation, and routine business including finals-week library-hours funding and an early suicide-awareness discussion.
documents.extract: Miles and Koehler disagree with Luttrell's remarks on the need for a separate Judicial Council adviser.

leaders.name: Jay Todd Richey
leaders.note: Re-elected. In office for Resolution 6-17-S, the reparations resolution, which passed 19-10-1 on 18 April 2017 and drew national coverage. Richey publicly framed it as a conversation starter; President Gary Ransdell stated within days that WKU would not adopt it.

sources.label: Bowling Green Daily News, Apr 2017 (archived copy)

profile: His re-election made him WKU SGA's first two-term president since 1988 and one of only three since 1974. Over his two terms he led the creation of three new committees, Sustainability, MyCampusToo and SAVES (Standing Against Violence and Ending Self-harm), revamped SGA's website, authored nine bills and resolutions, and represented students on the Board of Regents, the University Senate and the presidential search committee that chose WKU's 10th president. A Herald profile in March 2017 described a president who arrived late to office hours from overrun meetings, fielded budget questions and calls from the chief of police, and admitted he still struggled with low self-esteem.

In a farewell letter published as his term ended, Richey wrote that fighting for college affordability had been a personal priority: SGA rallied at the Kentucky Capitol and lobbied the General Assembly against university budget cuts, and he chaired the Board of Student Body Presidents of Kentucky. He cited expanded services for military and veteran students, the Rave Guardian safety app, WKU's first eSports program, an SGA Voter Empowerment Initiative that registered hundreds of voters, new SGA scholarships including one for students with disabilities, and helping select president Tim Caboni. His successor Andi Dahmer took the oath of office on May 2, 2017.

events.title: Resolution 6-17-S passes 19-10-1
events.body: Senators Andrea Ambam and Brian Anderson wrote a resolution supporting reparations for Black students, calling for full and free access to WKU for all Black people and asking for a task force on test-optional and geographically weighted admissions. Modelled on a resolution passed at Wisconsin-Madison earlier that year.

events.title: President Ransdell rejects the resolution
events.body: National wire coverage followed, along with a Tucker Carlson interview with Ambam and a wave of fabricated headlines claiming WKU had granted free tuition. Ransdell stated within days that it was not a university position. Both authors described it as a conversation starter.

events.title: Richey re-elected SGA president in high-turnout election
events.body: WKU students re-elected Jay Todd Richey as SGA president and elected Kate Hart as executive vice president in one of the highest-turnout elections in the association's history, with 2,442 voters. Richey defeated opponent Braxton Powell with 64 percent of the overall vote. Powell was elected a junior senator and his running mate Zach Jones a senior senator.

events.title: Senate rejected 2.0 GPA bill, backed housing diversity
events.body: SGA rejected a bill that would have let students vote to lower the organization's GPA requirement from 2.5 to 2.0, a change supporters said would make the body more representative; a Twitter poll found 61 percent of respondents opposed it. The senate also approved a resolution asking Housing and Residence Life to address the lack of diversity in on-campus housing under the university's 10-year housing plan.

events.title: SGA created Jonesville scholarship fund
events.body: The senate created a scholarship memorializing Jonesville, the African American community founded by freed slaves in the 1870s that stood on land now occupied by Smith Stadium, Nick Denes Field and Downing Student Union until WKU bought and demolished it in the late 1960s. Senators debated whether the award should go only to African American students as repayment for Jonesville's condemnation or be opened to all minority students.

events.title: SGA backed prioritizing faculty raises over construction
events.body: The senate passed a resolution supporting future faculty salary increases, written to mirror a concurrent resolution headed to the Faculty Senate and proposed by Administrative Vice President Hannah Neeper and Chief of Staff James Line. The resolution urged that salary increases be prioritized over future construction or renovation projects, citing WKU's second-to-last ranking in faculty pay among its 19 benchmark institutions in 2015 and a survey in which 57 percent of faculty rated their morale as poor or very poor.

events.title: Andi Dahmer elected to succeed Richey
events.body: Louisville sophomore Andi Dahmer, a senator and chair of the MyCampusToo committee, was elected the next student body president, winning 930 of 1,579 votes cast against Kenan Mujkanovic's 305 and Lily Nellans's 212. Her running mates Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry won executive vice president and administrative vice president. Dahmer said she would start with legislation on study abroad affordability and sensitivity training to improve retention among marginalized groups.

events.title: Ransdell condemns racist incidents after notes, vandalism
events.body: In the weeks before, racist notes had been left in a WKU assistant dean's office and a racial slur was scratched into a student's car following a parking dispute. President Gary Ransdell called the acts "cowardly" and "heinous," said they did not reflect the university's values, and called for campus dialogue on intolerance.

events.title: Senators raise campus racism at first fall meeting
events.body: At the third meeting of the 15th Senate, student speakers Jeb Veeck, Francisco Serrano and Spencer Wells addressed the recent racist incidents on campus. Veeck suggested a Q&A session on the issue and Serrano urged senators to help end racism on campus.

events.title: Two SGA members resign amid racism complaint; investigation nullified
events.body: After Chief Justice Cody Cox told the Oct. 11 senate meeting he had received a complaint that several SGA members made racist remarks, senator Braxton Powell and justice John McKinney resigned the next morning, citing scheduling conflicts and personal reasons respectively; neither confirmed, denied, nor acknowledged any link between the resignations and the complaint. The Judicial Council's planned investigation was dropped because the students in question had already left SGA, and the organization never released the identities of the accused or the nature of the alleged remarks. President Richey and MyCampusToo chair Helen Vickrey issued a statement the next day condemning the alleged acts.

documents.title: Senate minutes, 13 September 2016
documents.summary: Minutes of the third meeting of the 15th Senate, recording the fall 2016-17 executive cabinet, Senate officers, and committee chairs under President Jay Todd Richey's second term, plus early senator discussion of that fall's racist incidents on campus.
documents.extract: Senators address recent racism on campus; full cabinet and committee roster.

profile: Andi Dahmer, a Louisville sophomore who had served as a senator and chair of the MyCampusToo committee, was announced as the next student body president shortly after midnight on April 19, 2017, winning 930 of the 1,579 votes cast against Kenan Mujkanovic's 305 and Lily Nellans' 212. Her running mates Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry were elected executive vice president and administrative vice president, and Dahmer entered office already drafting legislation aimed at improving retention, making study abroad more affordable and supporting sensitivity training.

Her year in office was marked by internal division. The senate saw longer debates, more than 15 proposed constitutional amendments compared with about 10 the year before, and an emergency Judicial Council meeting on Jan. 29, with contention peaking around the DACA debates of October and November 2017, when the senate failed a clean DREAM Act resolution before passing a resolution supporting DACA students. Dahmer said the year had become "almost toxic in nature" and blamed partisan ideologies brought into what was supposed to be a nonpartisan organization.

In April 2018 Dahmer told the Herald she had endured months of harassment as president and student regent, including senators cursing at her in the SGA office, a group message thread of eight people called the "Justice Friends" that wished her physical harm, and a profane note left on her car on Feb. 9 that prompted a police report. Of the note she said, "That's when I really started fearing for my life on this campus." Her residence hall director reported her case to the Title IX office, which found it did not meet the legal standard for harassment; it was processed instead through the Office of Student Conduct, which issued no-contact orders against two senators, and she did not seek reelection.

In 2018 Dahmer, whose full name is Loandria "Andi" Dahmer, sued WKU, university president Timothy Caboni, director of student activities Charley Pride and assistant general counsel and Title IX coordinator Andrea Anderson, alleging sex-based discrimination and harassment by fellow SGA members, negligence by the university in responding to it, and that Caboni retaliated against her by declining to write a letter of recommendation for a Rhodes Scholarship application. U.S. District Judge David Hale granted the defendants summary judgment in March 2021, finding WKU had not been deliberately indifferent and that the incidents were not severe enough to constitute actionable harassment; the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals partially revived the case in 2022, directing the district court to consider whether student-on-student harassment had occurred before February 2018. The parties settled in January 2024, with WKU's insurance carrier paying Dahmer $10,000 and the university's attorney describing the payment as nominal and made without any admission of wrongdoing.

events.title: First senate meeting passes constitutional amendments
events.body: SGA held its first senate meeting of the year and approved three of five proposed constitutional amendment bills, which then went to the student body for a vote in the fall elections. The passed bills added constitutional review duties to the Judicial Council, made the chief justice backup speaker of the senate, and required senators to post one office hour per week. Senators also debated Bill 5-17-F, which proposed limiting the legislative powers of the executive branch.

events.title: Dahmer condemned a blackface Halloween incident at senate meeting
events.body: President Andi Dahmer opened the eighth meeting of the Senate by telling members that a student had worn blackface to a Halloween party the previous weekend and that it was not acceptable. She also hosted student body presidents from other Kentucky universities on campus that weekend and reminded senators that Herald reporters were allowed into all university committee meetings.

events.title: SGA passes resolution supporting DACA students
events.body: At its Nov. 7 meeting the senate passed a resolution, co-authored by President Andi Dahmer and Francisco Serrano, standing in solidarity with WKU students who were DACA recipients. The measure passed 32-1 and was a revision of the clean DREAM Act resolution rejected the previous week, reframed to address only the WKU student community. Dahmer noted WKU was one of the last Kentucky schools to pass something of this nature.

events.title: SGA members rally in Frankfort for higher education
events.body: About 20 WKU SGA members joined roughly 100 students from Kentucky's public universities at the Kentucky Board of Student Body Presidents' annual Rally for Higher Education on the Capitol steps in Frankfort on Feb. 6. Dahmer said the board of student body presidents had been working consistently since August to plan the rally.

events.title: LGBTQ activists address senate after senator's remarks
events.body: Several LGBTQ student activists spoke to the senate on April 3 after Senator Dallas McKinney had cited the Bible on March 27, reading verses saying the "wicked" deserved death, as his reason for voting against Bill 13-18-S, which funded $250 for stoles for the Lavender Recognition Ceremony honoring LGBTQ graduates. The bill passed in the senate, and speakers including SGA member Brigid Stakelum and Diversity and Inclusion Committee Chair Mark Clark called the remarks dehumanizing and discriminatory.

events.title: Mayer wins presidency after disqualification reversed
events.body: Stephen Mayer was elected SGA president and student regent, with Garrett Edmonds as executive vice president and Harper Anderson as administrative vice president. Their MEA ticket had been disqualified on April 16 after a complaint over a Pepe the Frog meme in a campaign chalk drawing, but the Judicial Council reversed the disqualification to a suspension before results were announced. Mayer won 35 percent of the 2,378 votes cast in the presidential race, ahead of Conner Hounshell with 33 percent and Kenan Mujkanovic with 32 percent.

events.title: Dahmer details months of harassment
events.body: In a Herald investigation, Dahmer said members of SGA had cursed at her, called her derogatory names and exchanged group messages in a GroupMe called the "Justice Friends" wishing her harm over the fall and spring semesters, and that a profane note left on her car on Feb. 9 led her to file a WKU police report and avoid her residence hall for two weeks. Her case was reported to WKU's Title IX office, which told her the conduct did not meet the legal standard for harassment, and it was processed instead by the Office of Student Conduct, which issued no-contact orders against two senators.

events.title: Judicial Council censured PR committee chair over election-discrepancy complaint
events.body: At an emergency meeting, the Judicial Council took up a complaint public relations committee chair Will Hurst had raised at the Jan. 23 senate meeting, alleging the executive board failed its constitutional duty to advertise the fall election and citing a discrepancy in vote totals between constitutional amendments that passed and failed. The council found the executive board had complied with the constitution and issued a censure against Hurst; Dahmer said she was pleased the council had upheld the board's conduct. The censure was confirmed at the Feb. 6 senate meeting.

events.title: Dahmer joined national solidarity letter after Charlottesville
events.body: President Andi Dahmer was one of more than 120 college student body presidents nationwide who signed an open letter backing the University of Virginia after the violent Charlottesville protests, and said developing campus-wide "cultural competency training" was a goal for the semester.

events.title: Senate passed a required sexual assault education resolution, 29-1
events.body: Resolution 1-17-F, co-authored by public relations chair William Hurst, S.A.V.E.S. chair Ashlyn Jones and three senators, supported adding a one-credit-hour sexual assault education course to freshman colonnade requirements, arguing existing options like HAVEN and Green Dot carried no penalty for skipping them. The senate also funded a "No-Shave November" beard contest and fixed the timing of constitutional-amendment elections in the bylaws.

events.title: Senate backed LGBTQ health curriculum, chair swap on Diversity committee
events.body: The senate unanimously passed a resolution supporting integrated LGBTQ health curriculum in WKU's medical education programs, co-authored by diversity and inclusion chair Mark Clark, chief of staff Conner Hounshell and administrative vice president Kara Lowry. Clark was approved as the committee's new chair after Corey Newsome stepped down over scheduling conflicts.

events.title: Dahmer announced she would not seek reelection
events.body: Citing tension in the senate that she called "almost toxic in nature" and that she attributed to partisan ideology in a body meant to be nonpartisan, Dahmer said in a Facebook post she would not run again and endorsed Conner Hounshell for president alongside Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry, seeking reelection to their executive vice president and administrative vice president seats.

events.title: Caboni announced Title IX review after Dahmer harassment report
events.body: University president Timothy Caboni said he would convene a faculty-staff-student committee, co-chaired by sociology professor Lauren McClain and counseling official Karl Laves, to review WKU's Title IX, Equal Employment Opportunity and Office of Student Conduct processes following the Herald's report on the harassment Dahmer said she experienced. President-elect Stephen Mayer called Dahmer "a super strong woman" and said he did not stand for harassment or sexual assault.

senate.note: This was the 16th Senate. Under the constitution as amended spring 2017, the Senate was composed of 36 seats: 3 each for senior, junior, sophomore and freshman classes, 2 graduate, 1 ESL international student, 1 Gatton Academy, 6 academic-college, and 14 at-large.

leaders.name: Stephen Mayer
leaders.note: Confirmed by an independent WKU record outside the plaque: the University Senate's Nov. 15, 2018 meeting agenda lists him under reports as "SGA President: Stephen Mayer."

sources.label: WKU University Senate meeting agenda, 15 Nov 2018

profile: Mayer was elected SGA president and student regent in April 2018 on the MEA ticket with Garrett Edmonds and Harper Anderson, taking 35 percent of 2,378 presidential votes against Conner Hounshell's 33 percent and Kenan Mujkanovic's 32 percent; 2,447 students voted overall. His ticket won only after the Judicial Council reversed a disqualification it had imposed days before the election over the campaign's use of a Pepe the Frog meme chalked on campus sidewalks, downgrading the penalty to a campaign suspension.

A biology and chemistry double major who had served three semesters as a senator and studied at Harlaxton College, Mayer opened his term in September 2018 promising greater transparency from both the Board of Regents and SGA, and required senators to log a weekly office hour. As student regent he was an outspoken critic of WKU's fee structure, especially the $450 online academic fee, and opposed that year's 4 percent tuition increase, saying he did not see the need to put the financial burden "on the students' backs."

events.title: Senate rejected first Judicial Council nominee of the term
events.body: The senate voted 8-7-1 against confirming Wood Brown, a Pike fraternity member and law clerk, as associate justice of the Judicial Council, after Mayer said his constitutional duty required him to appoint whom he judged best despite recusing himself from the interview process; senators argued the Judicial Council's own top-ranked applicant, not Brown, should have been chosen. Mayer's next nominee, Alex Rivera, was confirmed the following week.

events.title: Academic and Student Affairs directorship filled after two failed tries
events.body: The senate confirmed Aubrey Kelly as Director of Academic and Student Affairs 24-3-4, three weeks into the term. Initial nominee Ashley Cox was not confirmed at the first meeting after senators questioned her committee attendance, then withdrew when a family member was hospitalized; her replacement, Anna McAvoy, failed confirmation 6-9-1 on Sept. 11 after a senator raised concerns about her scholarship-grading experience.

events.title: Senate asked WKU to cancel classes on Election Day
events.body: SGA unanimously passed Resolution 5-18-F asking the university to cancel classes on Nov. 6, 2018, so students could get to the polls, after a presentation by Francis Wilson of the get-out-the-vote campaign Reg 2 Vote, and approved $300 in support through Bill 7-18-F. The senate also passed Resolutions 1-18-F and 2-18-F, which asked WKU to strike code-of-conduct language barring students from refusing a direction from a university official and from audio recording student-faculty meetings. Mayer's nominee Alex Rivera was confirmed as associate justice of the Judicial Council 12-3 after an earlier nomination had failed.

events.title: First Year Village housing plan presented to SGA
events.body: Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds presented plans for a freshman First Year Village of two new pod-style residence halls at the bottom of the Hill, replacing Bemis Lawrence and Barnes-Campbell halls on the site of the Pearce-Ford Tower parking lot. The senate also approved Bill 6-18-F, funding a sustainability film festival, by a 21-4 vote with one abstention.

events.title: SGA created a first-generation student scholarship
events.body: The senate passed a bill by Campus Improvements Chair Matt Barr creating a recurring $2,000 scholarship for first-generation college students, approved 31-1. It also passed organizational aid Bill 11-18-F, sending $1,400 to Delta Sigma Theta, Phi Beta Sigma and the jump rope club, and allocated $100 to advertise the Campus Safety Walk.

events.title: Contested appointment and Identity Evropa denouncement ended the fall term
events.body: President Stephen Mayer's nomination of graduate student Emily Anne Pride, daughter of a former SGA adviser, to a vacated senate seat sparked about 90 minutes of debate before she was confirmed 17-9 with two abstentions. The senate then passed Resolution 10-18-F, supporting denouncement of the white nationalist group Identity Evropa and its attempts to recruit on campus, 28-0, and allocated $430 to the Black Leadership Academic Conference through Bill 24-18-F.

events.title: Resolution passed to relocate Confederate marker
events.body: After lengthy debate, the senate passed Resolution 1-19-S by a 29-1 vote with one abstention, calling for the marker near the Kentucky Museum identifying Bowling Green as the Confederate capital of Kentucky to be relocated to a display inside the museum. Authors Kara Lowry, Conner Hounshell and Symone Whalin argued the marker was a reminder of oppression against people of color, and Mayer said the resolution would go to the WKU Administrative Council. The senate also allocated $1,000 to send the Mock Trial team to a national tournament.

events.title: Mayer declined to seek re-election as election codes were set
events.body: Mayer announced he would not seek re-election because he was applying to medical schools, and the senate approved the spring 2019 election codes 31-1, with campaigning to begin April 1 and voting on TopNet April 15-16. Chief Justice Jacob McAndrews announced he would resign from the Judicial Council to run for elected office. The senate also passed four spending bills, rejected a change to senator office-hour rules and tabled a bill creating a first-generation senate seat.

events.title: Transparency resolution passed after the dean's resignation
events.body: A week after Snyder's sudden resignation, the senate passed Resolution 4-19-S by a 30-2 vote, calling on top university officials to provide explanations for major decisions. In the same meeting it rejected Mayer's Judicial Council nominee Wood Brown 17-11, created a senate seat for first-generation college students 33-0, and passed a resolution 33-0 asking WKU to let students' preferred names appear on class rosters, IDs and email addresses, a measure brought by the Transgender Non-Binary student organization.

events.title: No-confidence vote and provost's resignation shook the university
events.body: After Snyder was asked to resign as Potter College dean on March 26, protests from faculty, staff and students led the University Senate to an unprecedented vote of no confidence in Provost Terry Ballman on April 4, and she resigned the next day. Ogden dean Cheryl Stevens was named acting provost, and days later the Comprehensive Academic Program Evaluation committee recommended suspending 101 of WKU's 380 academic programs.

events.title: WGK ticket won the spring executive elections
events.body: The ticket of Will Harris, Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic won the spring SGA elections, defeating the ticket of Asha McWilliams, Jacob McAndrews and Symone Whalin. Harris was elected student body president to succeed Mayer, Edmonds was re-elected to a second term as executive vice president, and Mujkanovic defeated Whalin for administrative vice president, with results announced at SGA's election party on April 16.
